name: Habitica
tagline: A to-do list and habit tracker dressed as a pixel-art RPG, where skipping your dailies costs you hit points.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanical core is embarrassingly simple: habits, dailies, and to-dos that pay out XP and gold, plus HP damage when you miss. An agent can build that loop, a streak counter, and a leveling curve in one session, and the free tier of the real thing already covers most solo use anyway. What breaks is everything social and everything cosmetic: parties, boss fights where your friend's missed dailies hurt you, guilds, challenges, and the decade of sprite art and quest writing that makes the numbers feel like a game. There is also no phone app, and a habit tracker you cannot open in a queue is a habit tracker you stop opening. Buildable, genuinely useful, but you are shipping the spreadsheet and skipping the game.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you check off habits, dailies, and to-dos, and a character gains XP, gold, and levels or takes damage when you miss.
requirements: A place to run it (laptop, home server, or a small VPS)
Willingness to open a browser tab instead of an app icon
whatYouLose: Parties and boss battles, the only part that adds actual social accountability
Guilds, challenges, and other people's habit lists to copy
The pixel art, pets, mounts, and gear that make the reward loop feel like a reward
Real iOS and Android apps with reminders and widgets
Years of accumulated avatar, streak, and gear history if you are already deep in
moatNotes: Habitica is open source, so the honest ceiling on the DIY build is not the code, it is that nobody else is standing in your dungeon.
whyPeopleStillPay: Most people do not pay, which is the point: the free tier is the product and the subscription buys gems, cosmetic pets, and the warm feeling of funding a nonprofit-ish open source project. The ones who do pay are usually deep in a party that expects them to check in, and that expectation is the actual product. A solo tracker you wrote yourself has no one to disappoint.
notes: The RPG math is trivial; the reason you keep doing your dailies is usually a person in your party, not the number.
prompt:
Build a single-user, self-hosted gamified habit tracker. Local first, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 (App Router, TypeScript) with Tailwind CSS
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, schema managed with Drizzle ORM, db file at ./data/app.db
- Server Actions for all mutations, no separate API layer
- Zero auth: assume one user on a trusted network. Read an optional APP_PIN from .env and if set, gate the app behind a single PIN cookie. Nothing else in .env.

Data model:
- tasks: id, type ('habit' | 'daily' | 'todo'), title, notes, difficulty ('trivial'|'easy'|'medium'|'hard'), dueDays (bitmask of weekdays, dailies only), dueDate (todos only), createdAt, archivedAt
- completions: id, taskId, completedOn (date), delta (xp/gold awarded)
- character: single row with level, xp, hp, maxHp, gold, streakBest

Game rules, implement exactly:
- Completing a task awards XP and gold scaled by difficulty (trivial 1, easy 2, medium 4, hard 8 as the multiplier base).
- Level up when xp crosses a curve of round(25 * level^1.6); carry the remainder, restore HP to max on level up.
- Habits can be checked multiple times a day and pay diminishing returns after the third check that day.
- Dailies reset at a configurable day-start hour (default 4am local). A cron-free approach: on each page load, run a catch-up routine that scores every missed daily since last visit and subtracts HP per miss, scaled by difficulty.
- HP hitting 0 means one lost level, xp reset to 0, HP back to max. Log it in a deaths table.
- Track current and best streak per daily.

UI:
- One main page: character bar (level, XP bar, HP bar, gold) on top, then three columns for Habits, Dailies, To-Dos. Click to complete, long-press or a kebab menu to edit or archive.
- A /history page with a 12 week heatmap per daily and a plain list of level ups and deaths.
- Ship a web app manifest and icons so it installs as a PWA on a phone. Do not attempt push notifications.

Explicitly out of scope: parties, guilds, challenges, chat, quests, pets, mounts, gear, avatars, a shop, or any multiplayer. No third party services.

Include a seed script with 3 habits, 4 dailies, and 2 todos, a README with setup in under ten lines, and a `npm run backup` script that copies data/app.db to ./backups with a timestamp.
